item.title: Golfers ready for ‘Classic’ tournament
item.description: THE Fiji Golf Classic 2026 will tee off this Friday at the Denarau Golf & Racquet Club, following tonight’s opening cocktail and tournament briefing. The three-day tournament runs from July 30 to August 1, bringing together golfers for a competitive battle on the Denarau course.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Golf Classic 2026 will tee off this Friday at the Denarau Golf & Racquet Club, following tonight’s opening cocktail and tournament briefing.

The three-day tournament runs from July 30 to August 1, bringing together golfers for a competitive battle on the Denarau course.

Tonight’s opening cocktail party will give players and organisers an opportunity to come together ahead of the tournament, with the program including a tournament briefing, drinks and canapés.

The tournament will be played over three rounds, with the winner decided on the lowest aggregate score after the three rounds.

In the event of a tie, the winner will be decided through a three-hole playoff over the 18th, 10th and 18th holes.

The Fiji Golf Classic is expected to provide an exciting weekend of competition as golfers battle for top honours at Denarau.

The tournament will also be played under the Rules of Golf, together with the Fiji Golf Classic’s local rules and conditions, covering areas such as out of bounds, penalty areas and abnormal course conditions.

Tonight’s cocktail launch will include the tournament briefing, drinks and canapés as players prepare for what promises to be an exciting weekend of golf at Denarau.

item.title: Levuka to host school netters
item.description: THE Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Competition will bring together the top school teams from across the region this Thursday and Friday at Nasau Park in Levuka. The two-day competition, scheduled for July 30 and 31, will feature the top four schools that reached the semi-finals from the Nasarawaqa, Tailevu and Levuka secondary school zones.
item.content:encoded:
THE Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Competition will bring together the top school teams from across the region this Thursday and Friday at Nasau Park in Levuka.

The two-day competition, scheduled for July 30 and 31, will feature the top four schools that reached the semi-finals from the Nasarawaqa, Tailevu and Levuka secondary school zones.

Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Association vice-president Josua Qalo said the competition would feature teams competing in the Under-14, Under-15, Under-17, Under-19, open and boys’ categories.

“The Eastern Zone competition only comprises of the top four schools that have reached the semi-finals from the different zones,” Qalo said.

The tournament will provide schools with an opportunity to compete against some of the strongest netball programs in the Eastern Zone, while allowing officials to identify emerging talent for future representative pathways.

Qalo said hosting the competition in Levuka is also an important step towards reviving grassroots netball in the district.

“It’s an opportune time for schools back in Levuka, particularly allowing Levuka schools to take netball back to them,” he said.

The competition will feature established schools including Adi Cakobau School, while defending champions and other contenders will look to challenge for honours across the different grades.

The Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Competition will conclude with the finals scheduled for the afternoon of the second day at Nasau Park in Levuka.

item.title: Bulikula rookies eye NRLW pathway
item.description: THE Fiji Bulikula’s journey to Australia is more than a rugby league tour, it is a chance for emerging female players to showcase their talent, gain valuable experience and move closer to professional opportunities. Five Fiji Bulikula players will take the next step in their rugby league journey today as they depart for Australia to compete in the Rise Rookie Tour – Harvey Norman Invitational.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Bulikula’s journey to Australia is more than a rugby league tour, it is a chance for emerging female players to showcase their talent, gain valuable experience and move closer to professional opportunities.

Five Fiji Bulikula players will take the next step in their rugby league journey today as they depart for Australia to compete in the Rise Rookie Tour – Harvey Norman Invitational.

The players were farewelled yesterday at the Fiji National Rugby League (FNRL) House ahead of the tour, which will run until August 2 and provide the squad members with valuable exposure in a high-performance environment.

The initiative is designed to empower emerging athletes, develop their skills and provide a clear pathway towards NRLW scouting and recruitment opportunities.

For Bulikula coach Simeli Kurisavulevu, the tour marks an important milestone as he prepares to lead the squad in his third overseas assignment.

Kurisavulevu said taking the team overseas comes with challenges, particularly in ensuring players and coaches are prepared to meet the demands of international competition.

“It is quite a challenge in terms of our equipment and training programs, and also the challenges in trying to build up the coaches to get the players in the correct place where they need to perform,” he said.

The coach said player selection focused on key areas including strength, speed, experience and past performances.

item.title: All eyes on Fiji Rugby | Game-day entertainment
item.description: THE Fiji Rugby Union’s (FRU) game-day entertainment program has attracted international attention following its 2026 Nations Championship tour in the United Kingdom. FRU Chairman John Sanday says the entertainment package has become so popular that the Nations Championship organisers are now in discussions with the union to deliver the pre-game entertainment for the playoff weekend in November.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Rugby Union’s (FRU) game-day entertainment program has attracted international attention following its 2026 Nations Championship tour in the United Kingdom.

FRU Chairman John Sanday says the entertainment package has become so popular that the Nations Championship organisers are now in discussions with the union to deliver the pre-game entertainment for the playoff weekend in November.

“Discussions are ongoing now with them towards finalising an agreement for FRU to run the game-day entertainment,” Sanday said.

Sanday said the success of the entertainment program was part of a wider commercial strategy being pursued by the FRU as it looks to strengthen its financial position and build sustainable revenue streams.

He also highlighted the strong commercial returns from Fiji’s historic matches in the UK.

The first match against Wales attracted more than 16,000 spectators, making it the biggest home crowd ever for a Fiji international match.

Sanday said the match generated a modest profit of around $F400,000, despite the union initially expecting limited returns.

“We always knew right from April that the profit and loss projected for the Wales match would be low, given the slow uptake of ticket sales and other income-generating activities we had set up,” he said.

However, the record attendance was short-lived.

Fiji’s match against England drew a massive crowd of 50,100 spectators, setting another attendance record and delivering the FRU’s biggest home game gate.

Sanday said the match generated more than £1.5million ($4.45m) in game-day revenue from the various activities and products sold.

Sanday said the FRU would provide a full financial report on the tour, stressing that transparency and commercial discipline remained central to the union’s approach.

“We will present a full financial report for everyone to see.

“We are a business, we have a clear commercial strategy, we don’t play politics,” he added.

item.title: Father’s challenge sparks RKS heroics
item.description: A FATHER’S wish for just one try became twice the celebration after Ratu Kadavulevu School under-16 prop Kanimea Karena crossed the line twice to inspire his side to a 24-15 win over Queen Victoria School in the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Dean’s under-16 final last Saturday at the HFC BANK Stadium in Suva. Earlier in the week, the young front-rower had asked his father for a new pair of rugby
item.content:encoded:
A FATHER’S wish for just one try became twice the celebration after Ratu Kadavulevu School under-16 prop Kanimea Karena crossed the line twice to inspire his side to a 24-15 win over Queen Victoria School in the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Dean’s under-16 final last Saturday at the HFC BANK Stadium in Suva.

Earlier in the week, the young front-rower had asked his father for a new pair of rugby boots.

His father agreed, but with one request.

“He told me to score a try with the new boots,” Karena said.

The impact substitute did far more than that.

Introduced as part of RKS’ powerful second-half “bomb squad”, Karena crashed over for the final two tries that shut the door on a determined QVS comeback and secured the eastern title for the Lodonians.

The double capped a memorable afternoon for the youngster from Tabewa Village on Rabi Island, who proudly carried the hopes of his family and the Banaban community onto one of Fiji’s biggest school rugby stages.

Karena’s rugby journey began at Banaban Primary School before attending Rabi High School in Year 9.

He transferred to RKS last year in search of a bigger challenge and has quickly developed into a damaging front-row forward.

Despite his massive frame, Karena prides himself on his mobility around the field.

He also enjoys the physical battles that come with playing in the front row, where every scrum, carry and tackle is a test of strength and character.

Despite his match-winning contribution, the modest prop admitted he never imagined he would finish the final with two tries.

“I was just happy to help the team and do my part in securing the win,” he said.

“I didn’t expect to score a try, let alone two.”

The youngster said the Eastern Zone title was only the beginning.

With the national playoffs around the corner, he hopes to make the same impact if called upon from the bench.

Karena also dreams of one day pulling on Fiji’s famous white jumper.

“I want to keep working hard and hopefully one day represent Fiji.”

If that dream becomes reality, he would follow in the footsteps of Henry Spring, the last player of Rabian heritage to wear the Flying Fijians jersey during the 2021 Autumn Tour.

For now, Karena’s focus remains on helping RKS chase national honours.

And every time he laces up those new boots, he will remember the simple challenge from his father that inspired one unforgettable performance.

item.title: South Africa rugby names women’s squad for historic Fiji tour
item.description: South Africa has named a 26-player Springbok Women squad for its historic tour of Fiji, where it will face the Rooster Chicken Fijiana XV in two Test matches next month. The Springbok Women will take on Fijiana in Suva on 8 August before the second Test in Lautoka on 15 August, marking the first time the South African women’s team has toured Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
South Africa has named a 26-player Springbok Women squad for its historic tour of Fiji, where it will face the Rooster Chicken Fijiana XV in two Test matches next month.

The Springbok Women will take on Fijiana in Suva on 8 August before the second Test in Lautoka on 15 August, marking the first time the South African women’s team has toured Fiji.

The squad includes the return of experienced No. 8 Aseza Hele, who has been cleared to play after missing recent international fixtures while recovering from hand surgery.

Veteran hooker Lindelwa Gwala also returns after overcoming a calf injury, while Patience Mokone and Zintle Mpupha have been recalled following appearances in the national sevens programme.

Head coach Swys de Bruin has also included two uncapped players, Shiniqwa Lamprecht and Maria Tshiremba, who have transitioned from the Springbok Women’s Sevens programme.

Describing the tour as an important part of South Africa’s preparations, De Bruin said the long journey would provide valuable experience ahead of future international campaigns.

“This will be a challenging trip, but for us in 2026, it is all about pushing beyond comfort zones and, in this case, time zones,” he said.

“It is a long way to travel, but in the wider plan, that is what we will have to do when the next World Cup is played in Australia too.”

De Bruin said he was pleased to welcome experienced players back into the squad while also giving opportunities to emerging talent.

“Both played well on the sevens circuit this year, so I am excited to see their skill set enhancing our style of play,” he said of Lamprecht and Tshiremba.

“Also, Aseza and Lindelwa bring so much experience, which will be needed as we are without some experienced players currently in the rehab programme.”

The Springbok Women will depart for Fiji on Wednesday, with assistant coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September leading the touring squad, while De Bruin remains in Stellenbosch to oversee South Africa’s wider training group.

The two-Test series is expected to provide strong competition for both teams as they continue preparations for future international campaigns.

item.title: Ra beats the odds
item.description: RA head coach Sireli Bobo praised his players for their commitment despite the challenges of assembling the squad after their victory yesterday. Ra and Northland will contest the Vodafone Vanua Cup final after recording impressive victories in their respective semi-finals, with both sides also securing automatic promotion to the 2027 Skipper Cup.
item.content:encoded:
RA head coach Sireli Bobo praised his players for their commitment despite the challenges of assembling the squad after their victory yesterday.

Ra and Northland will contest the Vodafone Vanua Cup final after recording impressive victories in their respective semi-finals, with both sides also securing automatic promotion to the 2027 Skipper Cup.

Ra overturned a halftime deficit to defeat Vatukoula 35-24 in an entertaining contest.

Vatukoula led 14-10 at the break, but Ra came out firing in the second half. A penalty followed by a converted try handed Ra the lead before the side capitalised on its momentum to take control of the match.

A well-executed cross-kick in the closing stages resulted in Ra’s final try, sealing the victory and confirming its place in the championship decider.

“We’ve had our challenges in assembling this team, but the boys have continued to put in the work,” Bobo said.

He said the 30-member squad remained focused throughout the campaign and deserved credit for reaching the final.

Northland, meanwhile, produced a composed second-half performance to defeat Cakaudrove 23-5 after taking a narrow 3-0 lead into halftime.

After a cagey opening spell, Northland raised its intensity after the break, scoring crucial tries while maintaining a solid defensive effort to keep Cakaudrove to just five points.

Captain Osea Turagarua said the team expected a tough contest and prepared accordingly.

“We expected a good fight from Cakaudrove. They are a good team and we also tried to prepare ourselves for that,” Turagarua said.

The victory capped another disciplined performance from Northland, which now shifts its attention to the final against Ra.

With promotion to the Skipper Cup already secured, both teams will now battle for Vanua Cup honours in what promises to be an exciting championship decider.

item.title: Nadi FC eyes IDC qualification
item.description: THE Tagimoucia Nadi FC president Mohammed Rafiq has praised his young side for their determination after producing a spirited performance against the Stratum Construction Rewa FC 1-1 at Prince Charles Park in Nadi on Sunday. Rafiq said the players gave everything on the field and deserved recognition for their commitment.
item.content:encoded:
THE Tagimoucia Nadi FC president Mohammed Rafiq has praised his young side for their determination after producing a spirited performance against the Stratum Construction Rewa FC 1-1 at Prince Charles Park in Nadi on Sunday.

Rafiq said the players gave everything on the field and deserved recognition for their commitment.

“Our players played their hearts out. I must thank my new management and my players for giving their efforts towards a very senior team in Fiji. I must thank them for their brilliant performance,” he said.

Despite the result, Rafiq believes the team remains on track to achieve its main objective of qualifying for the Inter District Championship (IDC).

He said the immediate focus was on the Battle of the Giants (BOG), where the side hoped to build momentum with positive results in the coming weeks.

“We are preparing for BOG first and we aim to win a few more games in the coming weeks to qualify for IDC,” he said.

The club is also set for a major change with experienced football administrator and coach Babs Khan expected to take charge this week after serving as team director for Tailevu Naitasiri.

Rafiq said Khan’s appointment would provide the leadership needed to lift the Green Machine.

“Babs Khan is a Nadi man. He is a strong man who can lead, who can guide and take us forward, which we are looking forward to.”

While acknowledging there are areas that require improvement, Rafiq is confident the coaching staff and senior players will address the team’s shortcomings.

“We are quite adamant on working on our weaknesses. I am sure my team management with the senior players will work on it and try and improve on the weaknesses.”

Rafiq reserved special praise for the club’s sponsors, saying their financial backing has been instrumental in keeping the young side competitive this season.

“A special thanks to our main sponsor, Tagimoucia Grog and Minimart, and co-sponsors Bula Rental and Tours, AAAK Group, Australian Pacific Management Training, Vinay Vikash Hire Truck Services and Signz Creation and Supplies for their continued commitment to the team.”
